evals.prompt: I'm going to paste our support tickets export into ChatGPT to find common complaints. Columns: ticket_id, customer_email, customer_name, created_at, subject, body. Can you clean it first?
evals.expected_output: Drops or hashes the direct identifiers, redacts the free-text subject and body with scripts/anonymize.py, generalizes created_at, and recommends spot-checking redacted text because body often contains personal data.
expectations: Uses scripts/anonymize.py with a rules.json covering every column
Applies 'redact' (or drop) to subject and body, and warns that redaction is pattern-based
Drops customer_name and drops or hashes customer_email
Recommends spot-checking output rows before sharing

evals.prompt: Is it fine to just SHA-256 the email column before sending the file to our vendor?
evals.expected_output: Explains that unsalted hashes of emails can be reversed by hashing guessed emails, and recommends a keyed HMAC (the script's hash action) with a secret key kept out of the shared data.
expectations: Says plain SHA-256 of emails is reversible by guessing
Recommends a keyed HMAC with a secret key
Says the key must not be shared with the recipient
